citation.title: DL-Scale: Deep Learning for model upgrading in topology optimization
citation.authors: Nikos Ath. Kallioras; Nikos D. Lagaros
citation.version_coded: version of record, author-uploaded full text

included.method_family: other: deep belief network with SIMP

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On the smallest tested mesh, DL-SCALE cuts the complete optimization time by 48.61% relative to plain SIMP, while lowering the reported compliance.
claim.location: Section 4, paragraph introducing Table 1 and first Table 1 row
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Table 1, 20,000-element case: 69.72 s SIMP / 35.82 s DL-SCALE = 1.9464; the paper states 48.61% time reduction. Other mesh sizes have larger reductions.
claim.alternatives: Table 1 shows time reductions of 60.15%, 65.56%, and 71.92% at 50,000, 75,000, and 100,000 elements; the abstract qualitatively says SIMP iterations and computational load are greatly reduced.

baseline.problem_size: Section 4, Table 1: one beam problem at 20,000, 50,000, 75,000 and 100,000 final finite elements; target final volume 35%
baseline.classical_iterations: Table 1: 219, 245, 277, 321 iterations at increasing mesh sizes; convergence stopping condition not stated
baseline.classical_time: Table 1: 69.72, 198.54, 342.51 and 540.44 s at increasing mesh sizes
baseline.ml_time: Table 1: 35.82, 79.12, 117.94 and 151.74 s at increasing mesh sizes; Section 4 says start-to-finish comparison includes reduced models and final SIMP fine-tuning
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; Section 3.2 describes two 100,000-element SIMP training problems producing 200,000 element input-output pairs
baseline.quality_metric: final compliance and target volume (Section 4, Table 1)
baseline.quality_gap: Table 1, 20,000 elements: compliance 18.13 DL-SCALE versus 18.48 SIMP (1.89% lower); other rows show 0.87-1.21% lower compliance

R1.evidence: Section 4 and Table 1 use the same 35% target volume and report slightly lower ML compliance, and the stated times include reduced runs and fine-tuning. Actual returned physical-field volume and classical stopping tolerance are not reported.

R2.evidence: Section 4, Table 1 gives both methods' total runtimes on the same problem sizes, but no R2(a)-(e) condition is established; solver and hardware are not specified.

R3.evidence: Section 3.2 reports 200,000 training pairs generated by two full SIMP problems; Section 4 reports inference-run savings, with neither generation nor training time or break-even uses.

R4.evidence: Section 4, Table 1 reports final compliance after SIMP fine-tuning at a 35% target volume, but does not give achieved volumes or failed/infeasible design rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: one test geometry at four element counts (Section 4, Table 1)

notes: The accessible article text is the author-uploaded version of record on ResearchGate. Training uses a different beam support/load setup from the Section 4 test beam [inferred from descriptions and figures], but only one test geometry is reported. The paper's timing comparison is stated to cover the full design process, including final SIMP fine-tuning.
